text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Some 141,007 orders to sell privatisation bonds have been registered on the market since the start of trading in August. So far only 24,485 bonds have been sold.

- Rudolf Mosny, a Slovak-born U.S. entrepreneur, has acccused the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund, of breaching an agreement on his prepurchase right on 79.4 percent in the eastern Slovak brewery Saris, where he already holds 18.7 percent. The NPF said it was only waiting for Mosny to pay for the stake.
- The Slovak government holds its regular session on Tuesday. The preliminary agenda does not include any major economic items.

- The private TV Markiza, which launched operations in September, held a 37 percent market share in the September- October period, compared with the two official channels STV 1 and STV 2, which together accounted for 32 percent.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The delay in submitting the 1997 draft budget to the parliament brings the risk that deputies could fail to approve the budget at the forthcomming session and that the country would have to adopt a provisional budget.

SME - The ruling coalition has submitted to parliament a new version of the controversial law on the protection of republic. Though the law is not on the agenda of the next session, starting December 4, it may be added to it by a proposal from a coaliiton deputy at the beginning of the session.
